fields.h1: Build a Trivia Quiz That Keeps Score for You
fields.hero_description: Build a trivia quiz that scores every answer, ranks teams after each round, and saves results to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Trivia Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Each trivia question has one right answer. Emergent builds the questions, the scoring, and the table that keeps every result.
fields.feature_1:
Rounds drafted around your topics

Name the rounds you want, such as science or 1990s music, and Emergent drafts 5 questions for each with 4 answer choices. Check every answer, then change any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Standings after every round

The app adds up each team's points when a round closes and puts the standings on the bar TV or the projector. Every team knows its place before the next round begins.
fields.feature_3:
A clock on each question

Set a limit per question, such as 30 seconds, and the app locks answers when it runs out. Every team gets the same window, and a late answer scores nothing for anyone.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Players answer on their phones, one question per screen. A team can share one phone or each player can answer alone, and Emergent sets no cap on how many people play.
fields.feature_5:
Every answer saved to your database

Each answer is a row in a database you own, with the player, the round, and the seconds taken. Sort by question to find the ones half the room missed, and replace them.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Run the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it after the season.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Hosts Run a Trivia Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
The Fact Hounds beat 10 teams with 27 of 30

Every Tuesday, 11 teams at Tidewater Tap play 6 rounds of 5 questions, one phone per team. After each round, the app totals the points and the bar TV shows the new order. Last week The Fact Hounds finished on 27 of 30, with Last Call Scholars second on 25.
fields.tab_content_2:
51 of 84 students miss one moon-phase question

On Fridays, 84 students in 3 science classes at Pinecrest Ridge Middle School take a 12-question review on their phones. The app flags any question missed by more than half of them. This week only the moon-phase question crossed that line, missed by 51 of 84, and it opens Monday's lesson.
fields.tab_content_3:
Omaha tops two other offices with an 11.4 average

Once a month, Calloway Freight runs a 15-question lunch quiz for 62 staff in Denver, Omaha, and Tulsa. Each office scores the average of its players, and a bigger office gets no head start. In March, Omaha's 17 players averaged 11.4 out of 15, and the app posted the win to the company Slack channel.
fields.tab_content_4:
A tie at 34 settled by one closest guess

The Maple Hollow Library fills its fall trivia night with 18 teams and 40 questions in 4 rounds. Shelf Awareness and the Barrowby Readers tied at 34. The tiebreaker asked how many books the library lent last year, and the answer was 61,240. Shelf Awareness guessed 58,000, closer than 52,500, and took first place.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Trivia Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write and run a trivia quiz that every table can finish and that ends with one clear winner.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Fix the rounds and their size
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write questions with one right answer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Order each round from easy to hard
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide who plays before you write a single question. A bar crowd wants rounds on mixed topics, while a science class wants questions on the unit it finished last week. Put the audience and the setting in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the quiz around them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the number of rounds and the questions in each before writing, such as 6 rounds of 5. Leave a short break after every round for scoring and refills. Teams then know how far through the night they are.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each question so one answer is right and none of the others can be argued. Name the exact thing you mean: the largest planet by size, a city in a named state. Vague wording turns a scoring break into a debate.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Open each round with an easy question and close it with a hard one. Every team scores early and stays in the game, and the last question of the round is the one that separates the tables.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Score by team or by player
fields.howto_step_5_des: Score by team when people play in groups, and by player in a classroom. When the teams differ in size, compare average scores instead of totals. Tell the players which method you use before the first round.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Hold back one question with a number answer, such as the year your town was founded. If two teams tie for first, ask it and give the win to the team whose guess lands closest. Check the number before the night.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test the quiz on two friends
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run the quiz past two friends before the night. Time how long one round takes, and rewrite any question they read two different ways. Then open the results table and confirm each answer scored the way you meant.

faq_plan.q: What is the best free trivia quiz online?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best free trivia quiz online?

prov.original: What is the best free trivia quiz online?

faq_plan.a: The best free online trivia quiz is one whose answers you can check. The 8-question quiz on this page is free to play, covers science and American landmarks, and explains every answer from a NASA, NOAA, or National Park Service page.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a trivia quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder: who plays, how many rounds, how many questions per round, and how scoring works. Emergent builds the quiz, the scoring, and a table of results from that prompt, and you change any question by prompting again. Check each answer against a source before the first game.

faq_plan.q: How do trivia quiz games score a joker round?
faq_plan.a: A joker round doubles a team's points for one round that the team picks before play starts. Announce the rule at the start, collect each team's pick with its first answer, and double only that round. Emergent builds the joker into the scoring when you name it in your prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a trivia quiz PowerPoint template run a live game?
faq_plan.a: A trivia quiz PowerPoint template puts the questions on screen, and the answers and scores still need a home. Pair the slides with an app that takes each team's answers on a phone, scores them as they arrive, and carries the totals between rounds.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a pub quiz trivia night have?
faq_plan.a: Plan 30 to 40 questions for a pub quiz trivia night, split into rounds of 5 to 10 with a break after each. Time one round in a trial run, then add or cut a round to fit the evening.

faq_plan.q: How is a trivia quiz different from a knowledge quiz?
faq_plan.a: A trivia quiz mixes topics for fun, and a knowledge quiz tests one subject a group has studied this month, such as a science unit. Both score one right answer per question. A knowledge quiz is worth reviewing afterward, question by question, to see what to teach again.

faq_plan.q: What should a trivia quiz maker do during a live game?
faq_plan.a: A trivia quiz maker should lock answers when a question's time runs out, total the points at the end of each round, and show the standings before the next round. On Emergent, the answers also land in a database you own. Next month's quiz can then drop the questions every team got right.

faq_plan.q: How do I pick topics for each round of a trivia quiz?
faq_plan.a: Give every round one topic and spread the topics across what your players know: a local history round, a music round, a science round. Avoid a whole round on one person's hobby, since one table could sweep it. Swap one topic each week to keep regulars interested.

faq_plan.q: How do I write who am I questions for a trivia quiz?
faq_plan.hint: Who am i trivia quiz questions and answers?
faq_plan.a: Write 3 to 5 clues about one person or thing, ordered from hardest to easiest, and reveal them one at a time. Award more points for a guess on an early clue, such as 5 points on the first and 1 on the last. Keep the last clue fair enough that every table can get it.

faq_plan.q: How many answer choices should a trivia quiz question have?
faq_plan.a: Four choices per question works well: one right answer and three plausible wrong ones of the same kind, such as four planets or four presidents. For a pub crowd, try open answers on the hardest round. Emergent puts no cap on how many players answer, and a packed room still fits in one quiz.

quiz.title: Trivia Quiz: 8 Questions on Space, Nature, and Landmarks
quiz.intro: Eight general-knowledge questions, each answer backed by a NASA, NOAA, or National Park Service page. Pick one answer per question; your score shows at the end.

questions.text: Which planet is the largest in the solar system?
questions.explanation: NASA's Jupiter facts page names it the largest planet in the solar system.

source.quote: Jupiter is a world of extremes. It's the largest planet in our solar system

questions.text: Which planet is the hottest in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Venus beats Mercury here: NASA puts its surface temperature at about 872 degrees Fahrenheit.

source.quote: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system, with surface temperatures about 872 degrees Fahrenheit

questions.text: The largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, is on which planet?
questions.explanation: NASA's Mars facts page names Olympus Mons, on Mars, as the largest volcano in the solar system.

source.quote: Mars is home to the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons

questions.text: Which animal is the largest on Earth?
questions.explanation: NOAA Fisheries names the blue whale as the largest animal on Earth.

source.quote: The blue whale is the largest animal on Earth

questions.text: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of which country?
questions.explanation: The National Park Service describes the statue as a gift of friendship from the people of France.

source.quote: A gift of friendship from the people of France to the United States

questions.text: Which of these presidents is carved into Mount Rushmore?
questions.explanation: The four faces are George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln.

source.quote: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln

questions.text: Which president signed the 1872 act that created Yellowstone National Park?
questions.explanation: Grant signed the Yellowstone National Park Protection Act on March 1, 1872.

source.quote: On March 1, 1872, President Ulysses S. Grant signed the Yellowstone National Park Protection Act into law

questions.text: Which words begin the inscription on the Liberty Bell?

options.text: Let Freedom Ring From Every Mountainside
Proclaim Liberty Throughout All the Land
Give Me Liberty or Give Me Death

questions.explanation: The full line on the bell reads Proclaim Liberty Throughout All the Land Unto All the Inhabitants thereof.

source.quote: Proclaim Liberty Throughout All the Land Unto All the Inhabitants thereof
